title: Session sidecar checkpoint protocol for interleaved stream metering
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Problem: Our current streaming metering pipeline attributes token credits based on a single canonical session record. In highly interleaved streams (client-side compress+batch, server-side function calls, midstream model switch, and client cancel) we observe transient overcharge or under-crediting when fragments arrive out of order or when attachments/sideband messages (e.g., image uploads) are replayed by clients. Goal: design and implement a lightweight 'session sidecar checkpoint protocol' that provides deterministic, idempotent checkpoints for in-flight streaming sessions to guarantee correct final attribution of input/output tokens and attachments while keeping latency and throughput targets. This ticket scopes the protocol design, reference implementation in the metering microservice, and a careful rollout plan with reconciliation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol defines stable checkpoint ids and idempotent ack semantics usable across HTTP streaming, WS, and multiplexed sessions
Final token tallies for interleaved test harness (see links) match ground-truth deterministic tokenizer run in >99.99% of randomized traces
No additional 95th%-ile latency regression on streaming API (>5ms) in canary load tests
Automated reconciliation run can detect and restore missing checkpoint events and produce refund/charge corrections with audit trail
Feature gated rollout available and observable via new Console dashboard: session-checkpointing-coverage per model/region
design_decisions: Introduce a small per-session sidecar state object stored in Redis (TTL 10m) with optimistic update using compare-and-swap via redis EVAL to avoid distributed locks
Checkpoint messages are small immutable records: {checkpoint_id, last_seq, token_digest, attachments_manifest_hash, model_variant_tag, idempotency_key}
Use token_digest (SHA256 over canonicalized token lengths) instead of full payload to keep checkpoints compact and privacy-preserving
Client and server both may emit checkpoints; the pipeline prefers server checkpoints when present. On conflict, deterministic tiebreaker is checkpoint_id lexicographic timestamp
Sidecar entries include a 'finalized' flag; only finalized checkpoints are used to finalize billing; unfinalized checkpoints are reconciled by background job after session TTL
implementation_notes: Add lightweight checkpoint producer in streaming-gateway that emits to metering-sidecar topic (kafka) for all streaming events; schema versioned
Metering service consumes checkpoints, validates token_digest against reconstructed tokenizer run for fragments seen, and stores final tallies to canonical billing table
On client reconnect with resume token, gateway must replay last acknowledged checkpoint_id to avoid double-counting; implement explicit resume handshake in WS protocol
Provide migration compatibility: if sidecar protocol not enabled for a customer, fallback to existing attribution logic; new behavior behind feature-flag per-tenant
Instrumentation: add metrics for checkpoint lag, reconcile-run corrections, finalization-rate, and percent of sessions with server-side checkpoints
rollout_plan: Week 1: Deploy protocol spec and unit tests, implement checkpoint producer in staging with feature flag off
Week 2: Canary enable for internal traffic (10%) and run randomized fuzz harness against canary to validate deterministic tallies
Week 3: Enable for select low-volume customers, run reconciliation job in 'dry-run' mode to produce audit-only corrections
Week 4: Start gradual enablement (25->50->100%) with automated rollback if correction rate > 0.05% or latency regressions exceed thresholds
Post-rollout: run 7-day reconciler to detect and apply any missed credit adjustments and publish incident summary to billing-ops channel
